question: True or false: US law lets the Treasury mint a platinum coin of any face value, even a trillion dollars?
answer: True. A 1996 provision meant for collectors' bullion coins lets the Treasury Secretary set the denomination of platinum coins, and it names no limit. In the 2013 debt-ceiling fight it was proposed as a way round Congress; the Treasury and the Fed declined. Notes face caps; this metal has none.
move: Read what a law says, not only what it was meant for.
trap: Assuming only the central bank, never the Treasury, can create money.
reference: United States Code, Title 31, section 5112(k), as added by Public Law 104-208, 1996
